answer.rationale: The 18% cut is hard-constrained and the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle; that removes renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms as cost-saving options for this cycle. memory_c2 (low-cost vendor onboarding, invoicing accuracy) is the direct evidence that the alternative supplier can deliver without a quality or billing surprise. memory_c3 (second source removed single-point-of-failure during shortage) matters because switching primary at day 71 with the line at 94% and no buffer would re-introduce exactly that risk if the new vendor is sole source. I pull both to confirm (a) the cost saving is real and durable, and (b) whether adding a second source is feasible inside the same contract action or must wait. If the archive confirms c2 and shows c3's dual-source structure can be layered onto the switch, I execute switch_primary_vendor with a contractual second-source clause embedded; if not, I still switch but flag the delivery-risk concentration for the next review rather than defer, because deferring past the 14-day expiry leaves zero primary coverage and is the worst delivery outcome available.
